top_stories.title: Accelerating the next phase of AI
top_stories.summary: OpenAI has published a blog post outlining its vision for the next phase of AI development, signalling strategic priorities and directions for the organisation. The post covers OpenAI's plans for scaling AI capabilities and deployment. This is a primary source announcement directly from OpenAI.

top_stories.title: Claude Code leak exposes a Tamagotchi-style 'pet' and an always-on agent
top_stories.summary: A leak of Anthropic's Claude Code source code has revealed an unreleased Tamagotchi-style AI 'pet' feature and an always-on background agent capability. The Verge reports the leak offers a rare glimpse into features Anthropic has been developing but not yet publicly announced. The findings suggest Anthropic is working on more persistent, ambient AI experiences.

top_stories.title: AI benchmarks are broken. Here's what we need instead.
top_stories.summary: MIT Technology Review examines why current AI benchmarks are failing to accurately measure real-world model performance, with many tests becoming saturated or gamed by developers. The article argues for new evaluation frameworks that better reflect how AI systems actually perform in practical settings. Experts quoted suggest the benchmark problem is now a serious obstacle to understanding genuine AI progress.

top_stories.title: The Pentagon's culture war tactic against Anthropic has backfired
top_stories.summary: MIT Technology Review reports that the Pentagon's attempt to leverage culture war rhetoric against Anthropic has failed to achieve its intended effect, with the strategy drawing wider scrutiny and criticism. The piece examines the intersection of AI safety, defence contracting, and political pressure on AI companies. It highlights the growing tensions between government actors and AI labs over values and deployment policies.

top_stories.title: Meta Adaptive Ranking Model: Bending the Inference Scaling Curve to Serve LLM-Scale Models for Ads
top_stories.summary: Meta's engineering blog details a new Adaptive Ranking Model that applies LLM-scale inference to its advertising systems, significantly improving ad relevance while managing computational costs. The post describes architectural innovations that allow large model capabilities to be deployed efficiently at Meta's advertising scale. This represents a concrete industrial application of frontier AI to a high-revenue commercial product.

further_links.title: You can now use ChatGPT with Apple's CarPlay
further_links.summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT has been integrated into Apple's CarPlay, allowing drivers to interact with the AI assistant through the in-car interface.

further_links.title: There are more AI health tools than ever—but how well do they work?
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review surveys the growing landscape of AI-powered health tools and finds that evidence for their real-world effectiveness remains thin and inconsistent.

further_links.title: Art schools are being torn apart by AI
further_links.summary: The Verge reports on the deep divisions emerging within art schools over how to address generative AI, with educators, students, and institutions holding sharply conflicting views on its role in creative education.

further_links.title: AI Has Flooded All the Weather Apps
further_links.summary: Wired examines how AI-generated summaries and features have rapidly proliferated across weather applications, raising questions about accuracy and the value added for users.

further_links.title: You can order Grubhub and Uber Eats 'conversationally' with Alexa Plus
further_links.summary: Amazon's upgraded Alexa Plus now supports conversational food ordering through Grubhub and Uber Eats integrations, marking a step forward in agentic AI assistants for e-commerce.

further_links.title: Shifting to AI model customization is an architectural imperative
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review argues that businesses must rethink their technical architecture to support AI model customisation, framing this shift as a strategic necessity rather than an optional upgrade.

further_links.title: Open to Work: How to Get Ahead in the Age of AI
further_links.summary: Microsoft's official blog offers guidance for workers on adapting to the AI-transformed job market, drawing on data about AI adoption and workforce trends.

further_links.title: Okta's CEO is betting big on AI agent identity
further_links.summary: The Verge's podcast features Okta's CEO discussing why managing the identity and security of AI agents is becoming a critical enterprise challenge as agentic AI deployments grow.

further_links.title: The Download: AI health tools and the Pentagon's Anthropic culture war
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review's daily briefing rounds up the latest on AI health tool evaluation and the ongoing controversy surrounding the Pentagon's stance toward Anthropic.

further_links.title: The ladder is missing rungs – Engineering Progression When AI Ate the Middle
further_links.summary: A blog post examines how AI tools are hollowing out mid-level engineering tasks, disrupting traditional career progression paths for software engineers.

ethan_mollick.title: Claude Dispatch and the Power of Interfaces
ethan_mollick.summary: Ethan Mollick explores how the interface through which AI is accessed fundamentally shapes what users are able to accomplish with it, using Claude's capabilities as a case study. He argues that the design of AI interfaces is as important as the underlying model, affecting the depth and usefulness of interactions. The post encourages readers to experiment with different modes of engaging AI tools to unlock their full potential.
